newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania $550 mln TANs F1-plus by Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania $550 mln TANs F1-plus by Fitch.

text.p: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's $550 million Tax Anticipation Notes, first series of 1996-1997, for bids on Oct. 2, are rated 'F-1+' by Fitch Investors Service.
The notes will be dated the date of delivery and be due June 30, 1997, with stated set-aside dates during May and June.

The notes are not general obligations, but are secured by current revenues levied and assessed for current purposes accruing to general funds during the current fiscal year; the amount necessary for principal and interest is specifically appropriated.

The Commonwealth intends to issue $200 million additional TAN's later in the fiscal year. Cash projections indicate a good margin of note security this year, although operating borrowing is expected to be 50% higher than 1995-1996's level. Operations in 1995-1996 were favorable, with revenues slightly over estimates.

However, the closing cash balance at June 30, 1995 was $888.5 million, about 20% below the originally anticipated level, due to several factors, including timing of federal aid and the use of opening surplus.

Budgetary surplus exceeded estimates, as costs were controlled. General fund surplus is projected to be largely depleted at the end of the current year. Cash operations in 1996-1997 expect deficits in five months, peaking at $649 million in February.

The general fund is expected to be in surplus by March and close with $1.0 billion. The total borrowing represents only 4.5% of revenues, 2.6% of cash flow and 22% of the amount legally allowed for operating purposes.

Projections indicate that the closing cash balance at June 30, 1997 will be $1.02 billion, which provides a 3.6% safety margin. Revenues in May and June, together with the estimated opening May balance would provide coverage of nearly 9 times for note principal.
In addition borrowable funds are projected to hold $614.3 million. Revenues for the first two months of the fiscal year are reported to be $10 million or 0.5% over estimates.
